notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is an apparently complete primary research article, Effort for Payment: A Tale of Two Markets, James Heyman and Dan Ariely, Psychological Science, Volume 15 Number 11, printed pp. 787–793, copyright 2004. Title, authors, journal, year and pagination match the neutral original reference. The DOI is not printed in this text, so DOI identity cannot independently be confirmed from this source. Source URL names the authors' PDF. No local source PDF was supplied, so no rendering or network acquisition was performed. Only the original side and three listed fields are assigned; replication/reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Target ambiguity: no definition links supplied Study label 1a to a particular source contrast. Do not equate that label with Hypothesis 1a without independent evidence. Candidate test statistics from p. 789 (all F, retained as printed, no effect conversion): Cash low versus medium (Hypothesis 1a): F(1, 607), value 5.03; p < .001. Candy low versus medium (Hypothesis 1b): F(1, 607), value 0.25; p = .81. Compensation level by payment form interaction (Hypothesis 1): F(1, 607), value 3.44; p < .001. Cash low versus no-payment control (Hypothesis 1c): F(1, 607), value 4.65; p < .001. Candy low versus no-payment control: F(1, 607), value 0.2; p = .84. Difference in low-payment reaction across markets: F(1, 607), value 4.53; p < .001. Monetized candy versus cash: F(1, 607), value 1.27; n.s., no numerical p. Monetized candy versus candy: F(1, 607), value 3.36; p < .01. Monetized candy low versus medium: F(1, 607), value 3.48; p < .001. Monetized candy low versus no-payment control: F(1, 607), value 3.84; p < .001. The canonical parse renders equality signs as 5 in these statistics; quotes retain literal source text. Printed same-test p bounds are retained even when the F/p combination appears unusual; no recalculation. Candidate recruitment count 614 is not promoted to analytic N. No group sum is possible from explicit final group counts; no arithmetic performed. All analyses are described in footnote 3 as planned contrasts within analyses of variance. Table 1 specifies design/payment conditions, not final cell counts.
